items.abstract: <jats:p>Highlights• Introduces SPBA: the first patch-wise backdoor for 3D point clouds.• Employs curvature-based scoring to select imperceptible complex patches.• Applies patch-wise spectral triggers (GFT) to minimize distortion and cost.• Demonstrates superior trade-off in effectiveness, stealthiness, and robustness.Stealthy Patch-Wise Backdoor Attack in 3D Point Cloud via Curvature AwarenessBackdoor attacks pose a severe threat to deep neural networks (DNNs) by implanting hidden backdoors that can be activated with predefined triggers to manipulate model behaviors maliciously. Existing 3D point cloud backdoor attacks primarily rely on sample-wise global modifications, which suffer from low imperceptibility. Although optimization can improve stealthiness, optimizing sample-wise triggers significantly increases computational cost. To address these limitations, we propose the Stealthy Patch-Wise Backdoor Attack (SPBA), the first patch-wise backdoor attack framework for 3D point clouds. Specifically, SPBA decomposes point clouds into local patches and employs a curvature-based imperceptibility score to guide trigger injection into visually less sensitive patches. By optimizing a unified patch-wise trigger that perturbs spectral features of selected patches, SPBA significantly enhances optimization efficiency while maintaining high stealthiness. Extensive experiments on ModelNet40 and ShapeNetPart further demonstrate that SPBA surpasses prior state-of-the-art backdoor attacks in both attack effectiveness and resistance to defense methods. The code is available at https://github.com/HazardFY/SPBA.</jats:p>
title: Stealthy Patch-Wise Backdoor Attack in 3D Point Cloud via Curvature Awareness

items.abstract: <jats:p>In federated learning (FL) systems, multiple defense mechanisms are deployed to mitigate threats posed by backdoor attacks. Consequently, attackers are compelled to adopt stealthy attack strategies to evade these defenses. However, stealthy attacks face a critical challenge in real-world deployment: the server acts as a black box for attackers, who cannot determine whether their attacks have successfully evaded defense mechanisms or maintained satisfactory backdoor performance after evasion. Excessively pursuing stealth will inevitably degrade attack intensity, leading to a suboptimal attack success rate (ASR). This creates an inherent trade-off: enhanced stealth comes at the cost of compromised backdoor performance, further exacerbating the difficulty of stable and effective attacks under black-box server constraints. To address this, we propose BANAR ({\bf {Ba}}ckdoor SO{\bf {NAR}}), a proactive and feedback-driven stealthy backdoor attack inspired by active sonar systems. The attacker periodically embeds BANAR signals into malicious updates and infers defense activation by analyzing the global model. Furthermore, BANAR enables adaptive adjustment of stealthiness for subsequent attacks. This mechanism enables BANAR to trade off between stealth degree and attack strength. Experiments show BANAR detects defense activation with 98% accuracy and reduces true positive rates of state-of-the-art defenses by approximately 56%. BANAR maintains a high ASR even under defenses, comparable to that in undefended scenarios, highlighting its capability to preserve attack efficacy while significantly enhancing stealth.</jats:p>
title: BANAR: Self-Feedback Stealthy Backdoor Attack in Federated Learning
